scan.method: First real-use run of Capability Radar 0.1.0. One assistant session following skills/scan/SKILL.md. Stack-first: Claude and ChatGPT release notes checked before the market. Web search (standard) per lane; GitHub repo pages and commit pages fetched for repo-backed candidates; support.claude.com and claude.com fetched. The session's network policy blocked direct fetches of most other hosts (help.openai.com, circleci.com, techcrunch.com, implicator.ai), so those pages were read through the search tool; each source's note says 'fetched' or 'search-read'. The GitHub REST API was not available, so release dates came from commit pages where readable. Not an exhaustive census.

candidates.name: Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io)
candidates.job: write a Skill once (SKILL.md folder) and run it in both Claude Code and Codex, the two coding agents already owned
candidates.description: Open SKILL.md format for packaging procedures; donated by Anthropic to the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) on 2026-10-22. Codex, ChatGPT, Copilot and other agents implement it.

sources.note: search-read; spec site, cited by the announcement
search-read; Codex skill format and trust tiers

candidates.evidence_notes: independent implementations by several vendors (Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot) of the same format; this is evidence of portability, not of any one skill's quality
candidates.privacy: skills run inside the host agent with its permissions
candidates.permissions: a skill can ship scripts that run with the agent's tool access
candidates.reason: Any Skill authored for this profile should target the open format so it runs in Claude Code and Codex alike; no install or cost.
candidates.reverify_trigger: AAIF governance or format change; new SKILL.md spec version

candidates.name: Anthropic Agent Skills (anthropics/skills)
candidates.job: ready-made document Skills (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf) and the skill-creator for file and document work inside coding agents
candidates.description: Anthropic's public Skills repository: example and document skills plus templates; the document skills are source-available, others Apache-2.0.
candidates.evidence_notes: official repo demonstrates the capability; no independent quality measurement found
candidates.cost: free; runs on an existing plan
candidates.permissions: document skills run bundled Python scripts
candidates.reason: Claude apps already use these for file creation; the gain is bringing the same document handling into Claude Code/Codex sessions. Try on one real PDF/xlsx job.
candidates.reverify_trigger: license change of the document skills; new document skill added

candidates.name: Superpowers (obra/superpowers)
candidates.job: structured coding workflow for agents: brainstorm, plan, test-first implementation and subagent-driven development
candidates.description: Skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents; supports Claude Code, Codex CLI/App, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI and others.
candidates.maintenance_notes: 686 commits on main; commit dates not readable in this session
candidates.evidence_notes: README and roundup claims only; no independent measurement of better outcomes; roundups are affiliate-style
candidates.permissions: skills instruct the agent to run tests, create branches and dispatch subagents
candidates.reason: Very popular, but popularity is not evidence; native plan mode and subagents already cover part of this. Worth one A/B on a real feature build.
candidates.reverify_trigger: independent evaluation published

candidates.name: Humanizer (blader/humanizer)
candidates.job: edit drafts to remove recognizable AI-writing patterns so long-form writing reads as human
candidates.description: Single-file agent skill based on Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing' guide; detects and rewrites ~26-29 patterns.
candidates.evidence_notes: pattern list is grounded in a public guide, but no controlled study shows readers or detectors identify humanized drafts less often; mechanical pattern removal can hurt intentional style
candidates.reason: Directly targets the writing job and is the most-used option, but the gain is unproven; a blind A/B on real drafts is needed before relying on it.
candidates.reverify_trigger: major version or published evaluation

candidates.name: Caveman (terse-output skill)
candidates.job: cut output tokens by making the agent answer tersely
candidates.description: Skill that makes coding agents reply in compressed 'caveman' prose; companion command compresses memory files.

sources.note: search-read; independent re-measurements cited; direct fetch blocked

popularity.signal: viral in 2026; canonical repo not established in this scan

candidates.evidence_notes: project claims ~65% output reduction; three independent re-measurements found 12-23% output reduction, and output is ~0.6-2.5% of total spend; the skill adds ~1-1.5k input tokens per turn
candidates.reason: Measured savings target the smallest share of spend and can go net-negative; input-side context tools address the larger cost.
candidates.reverify_trigger: input-side compression results published

candidates.name: skill-creator evals and benchmark mode
candidates.capability: measuring whether an AI capability helps
candidates.job: write evals for a Skill and benchmark it (pass rate, time, tokens) with vs without the Skill before adopting it
candidates.description: Anthropic's skill-creator plugin gained Create / Eval / Improve / Benchmark modes in 2026.

sources.note: search-read; reports a related 'claude plugin eval' command in v2.1.269; not verified against official notes

candidates.evidence_notes: official description of the capability; no independent review of eval quality
candidates.reason: This is the owned tool for the benchmarks this scan says are needed (writing, workflow, token Skills). Use it to run the first A/B.
candidates.reverify_trigger: 'claude plugin eval' confirmed in official changelog

candidates.name: skills.sh directory and leaderboard
candidates.job: discover Skills by install count and recent activity
candidates.description: Vercel's open Skills directory with an install-telemetry leaderboard and 'npx skills add' installer.

sources.note: search-read; leaderboard is driven by installs it promotes

candidates.evidence_notes: official description; ranking is popularity, which is not evidence of quality
candidates.privacy: the skills CLI sends anonymous install telemetry
candidates.permissions: installed skills run with agent permissions
candidates.reason: Useful only as a discovery feed; studies found 13% of marketplace skills with critical issues, so never install from rank alone.
candidates.reverify_trigger: adds security review or provenance signals

candidates.name: Claude plugin directory and developer portal
candidates.capability: vetting third-party skills, plugins and MCP servers
candidates.job: find reviewed plugins/connectors (MCP + skills bundles) for Claude and Claude Code in one place, with safety-scanned submissions
candidates.description: Developer portal (2026-09-25) for submitting plugins to the Claude directory; submissions are auto-validated and safety-scanned; one discovery experience is rolling out across Claude and Claude Code.
candidates.evidence_notes: official announcement; review depth of the safety scan not documented
candidates.permissions: per plugin; MCP servers, hooks and commands can run code
candidates.reason: Prefer this reviewed source over random GitHub repos when a plugin is needed; it lowers supply-chain risk for every other plugin/MCP candidate.
candidates.reverify_trigger: unified Claude + Claude Code discovery ships

candidates.name: OpenAI plugin directory (ChatGPT and Codex)
candidates.job: enable packaged workflows (skills + app connections) in ChatGPT and Codex
candidates.description: Since 2026-07-09 the ChatGPT app directory is a plugin directory; plugins bundle skills, apps and app templates and work in ChatGPT and Codex.

sources.note: search-read; direct fetch blocked by session network policy

candidates.evidence_notes: official help-center description
candidates.cost: included; availability depends on plan, region and surface
candidates.privacy: per app; app approval does not override source-system permissions
candidates.reason: Owned; check which existing apps now ship as plugins with skills before adding any third-party automation.

candidates.name: Claude Code official LSP code-intelligence plugins
candidates.job: semantic code navigation (definitions, references) in Claude Code instead of grep, for fewer tokens and more precise edits
candidates.description: Official language-server plugins (typescript-lsp, pyright-lsp, and others for ~11 languages) in claude-plugins-official; each needs its language-server binary.

sources.note: search-read; independent benchmark on a ~149K-line TypeScript codebase; direct fetch blocked

candidates.evidence_notes: independent CircleCI benchmark: LSP ahead of grep on price and tokens across six tasks ($1.88 vs $2.02); gains larger on Sonnet than Opus; modest overall
candidates.cost: free; language servers use local RAM
candidates.reason: Owned, free and independently measured, but the saving was modest; confirm on a real repo of your own before keeping it on.
candidates.reverify_trigger: LSP enabled by default in Claude Code

candidates.name: Email and calendar connectors in ChatGPT and Claude
candidates.job: triage email and manage calendar from the assistant you already use
candidates.description: Both owned assistants ship first-party email/calendar connectors (e.g. ChatGPT added iCloud Mail and Calendar on 2026-10-27; Gmail/Google Calendar and Microsoft 365 connectors exist in both).

sources.note: search-read; 2026-10-27 iCloud entry; direct fetch blocked

candidates.evidence_notes: official release notes; no measurement of time saved
candidates.privacy: material: grants the assistant read (and possibly write) access to mail and calendar
candidates.permissions: OAuth scopes per provider; prefer read-only
candidates.reason: Covers the personal-productivity job with no new vendor; start read-only per the profile's privacy constraint.

candidates.name: ChatGPT Meetings plugin
candidates.job: record and summarize meetings from the ChatGPT desktop app
candidates.description: Meeting-notes plugin launched with ChatGPT Space around DevDay 2026; reported as a macOS desktop beta.

sources.note: search-read; Oct 7-8 entry mentions a Meetings plugin

candidates.evidence_notes: no official feature page found; details from secondary sources
candidates.privacy: material: audio is streamed to OpenAI (per a competitor's guide; unverified)
candidates.reason: Owned but beta and macOS-only; revisit when OpenAI documents data handling.
candidates.reverify_trigger: general availability or official privacy documentation

candidates.name: Skill and plugin security scanning
candidates.capability: vetting third-party skills, plugins and MCP servers
candidates.job: scan third-party skills and plugins for malicious content before they run
candidates.description: Claude Enterprise admins can auto-scan uploaded third-party skills and plugins (beta, 2026-08-06); directory submissions are also scanned.

sources.note: search-read; 3,984 skills audited; 13.4% with a critical issue; 76 malicious payloads

candidates.evidence_notes: risk is independently measured; scanner effectiveness is not
candidates.reason: Not available to an individual plan; until it is, manual review of any skill/plugin/MCP stays mandatory.
candidates.reverify_trigger: scanning reaches Pro/Max plans or Claude Code

candidates.name: Context7
candidates.capability: current library documentation for coding agents
candidates.job: give the coding agent current, version-specific library documentation instead of stale training data
candidates.description: Upstash's docs platform and MCP server/CLI; optional free API key for higher rate limits.

sources.note: fetched; latest releases dated 23 Oct, year not shown
search-read; top-5 in a Sept 2026 ranking

candidates.maintenance_notes: releases dated 23 Oct (year not shown on page)
candidates.evidence_notes: no independent measurement of fewer API hallucinations; docs are community-contributed and the backend is closed
candidates.privacy: library queries go to Upstash's service
candidates.reason: Targets a real coding failure (stale APIs) but only claims exist; compare against the agent's own web fetch on one library upgrade.
candidates.reverify_trigger: independent hallucination-rate comparison published

candidates.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
candidates.capability: browser debugging and automation for agents
candidates.job: let the coding agent inspect, debug and profile a live Chrome page (console, network, performance traces)
candidates.description: Official Chrome DevTools team MCP server and CLI for coding agents.
candidates.evidence_notes: official vendor docs; no independent outcome measurement
candidates.privacy: usage statistics on by default (opt out with --no-usage-statistics); performance tools may send trace URLs to Google CrUX
candidates.permissions: full control of a browser profile; avoid profiles with personal sessions
candidates.reason: Fills a real gap for front-end debugging in the coding job; telemetry defaults must be turned off first.

candidates.name: Playwright MCP
candidates.capability: browser debugging and automation for agents
candidates.job: browser automation for agents via the accessibility tree
candidates.description: Microsoft's Playwright MCP server; its README recommends the Playwright CLI + Skills for coding agents as more token-efficient.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs; vendor itself steers coding agents to CLI + Skills
candidates.reason: For this profile's coding work the vendor recommends the CLI + Skills path; MCP fits long-running browser loops only.

candidates.name: Serena
candidates.job: symbol-level code retrieval and editing for agents via language servers (40+ languages)
candidates.description: Open-source MCP toolkit giving agents IDE-like semantic tools; works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and IDEs.
candidates.evidence_notes: 'much more token-efficient' is a README claim; the widely quoted 98% figure belongs to a different project
candidates.reason: Claude Code's own LSP plugins cover the same job with independent evidence; Serena matters only if Codex needs the same capability. GPL-3.0 for the app.

candidates.name: serena-slim
candidates.job: smaller tool surface for Serena (29 tools grouped into 18)
candidates.description: Fork of Serena that groups tools to cut tool-schema context; claims 50.3% fewer context tokens.
candidates.evidence_notes: fork's own estimate; reduction is schema overhead, not retrieval
candidates.reason: Wrapper of Serena; Claude Code tool search already defers tool schemas.

candidates.name: context-mode
candidates.job: keep large tool outputs (logs, snapshots, API dumps) out of the agent's context by sandboxing them and returning summaries
candidates.description: MCP server + hooks that run tool output in a sandbox, index it in SQLite FTS5, and return only relevant snippets; supports ~18 agents.
candidates.evidence_notes: 98% tool-output reduction (315 KB -> 5.4 KB) is the project's own figure; no independent end-to-end task measurement
candidates.cost: free; Elastic License 2.0 (not OSI open source)
candidates.permissions: hooks intercept tool calls; MCP sandbox executes commands
candidates.reason: Targets the largest context drain (tool output, 60-80% of context per one guide); must be benchmarked for task success, not just bytes saved.
candidates.reverify_trigger: independent task-success benchmark

candidates.name: GitHub MCP Server
candidates.job: issues, PRs, code search and Actions from any MCP client
candidates.description: GitHub's official MCP server, local or hosted remote, with a read-only mode.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs
candidates.reason: The owned agents already reach GitHub through the gh CLI and native GitHub connectors; adds context cost without a new capability.

candidates.name: MCP 2026-07-28 specification and official registry
candidates.job: know which protocol version and registry future MCP servers and Skills should target
candidates.description: Largest MCP revision since launch: stateless protocol without the initialize handshake; roadmap adds agent identity and HTTP-native transport; official registry at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.
candidates.evidence_notes: official spec communication; some pages still label it a release candidate
candidates.reason: Not something to adopt; it decides how any future public tool from this profile should be built.
candidates.reverify_trigger: next spec revision or client support for stateless mode

candidates.name: Claude Code cloud sessions and scheduled tasks
candidates.job: run coding tasks unattended in the cloud and on a schedule, then review the result
candidates.description: Already in the profile's stack: cloud sessions and scheduled tasks in Claude Code.
candidates.evidence_notes: official product; owned
candidates.reason: Already owned; covers background coding execution. Nothing to add.

candidates.name: Codex cloud tasks and automations
candidates.job: parallel background coding tasks and scheduled Codex runs
candidates.description: Codex cloud tasks plus desktop-app automations (scheduled runs in a local project or worktree; need the machine awake).
candidates.evidence_notes: official academy page; details from a practitioner blog
candidates.privacy: local runs use the local sandbox settings
candidates.reason: Already owned; overlaps Claude Code scheduled tasks. Keep one as the default for scheduled coding work.

candidates.name: Claude Duet
candidates.job: proactive assistant that checks connected apps every few hours, sends a morning brief and flags what needs attention
candidates.description: Standalone Anthropic app (research preview from 2026-10-21) where Claude works as a proactive agent; asks consent before sending, paying, signing or deleting.
candidates.evidence_notes: official announcement; no independent hands-on reviews yet
candidates.cost: included in Pro/Max; background checks count against plan usage
candidates.privacy: material: reads connected email/calendar/apps on a schedule
candidates.permissions: connector scopes; consent gates for outbound actions
candidates.reason: Owned plan includes it, but it is a US waitlisted research preview; test once it graduates.
candidates.reverify_trigger: leaves research preview or opens outside the US waitlist

candidates.name: ChatGPT dots (always-on agents)
candidates.job: always-on personal agent with its own cloud computer and browser that keeps working toward goals
candidates.description: Launched at DevDay 2026-09-29 for Pro and Business Premium; one dot per user at launch; reaches apps via plugins.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs page exists; outcome evidence is launch coverage only
candidates.cost: ChatGPT Pro or Business Premium only
candidates.privacy: material: agent acts in a cloud browser with connected apps
candidates.reason: Plan-gated to Pro; overlaps Claude Duet and existing scheduled tasks. Revisit if the plan tier includes it.
candidates.reverify_trigger: available on Plus or multiple dots per user

candidates.name: Hermes Agent
candidates.job: self-hosted persistent agent that keeps memory, writes its own reusable skills and runs scheduled jobs across chat apps
candidates.description: Nous Research's open-source (MIT) agent; model-agnostic (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint); messaging integrations.
candidates.evidence_notes: '40% faster with 20+ self-created skills' is Nous's own figure; SkillsBench found self-generated skills do not help on average
candidates.cost: free; pay for the model endpoint
candidates.permissions: host tool execution and messaging accounts
candidates.reason: Interesting for persistent execution, but self-hosting an agent with host tool access conflicts with the profile's security constraint while owned scheduled tasks exist.
candidates.reverify_trigger: independent evaluation or security audit

candidates.name: OpenClaw
candidates.job: local always-on personal agent reachable from chat apps
candidates.description: Very popular open-source personal agent gateway; README says tools run on the host unless sandboxing is configured.

sources.note: search-read; nine CVEs in March 2026 reported

candidates.evidence_notes: adoption is huge, but evidence of job improvement is anecdotal; security record includes multiple 2026 CVEs and vendor advice against running on standard machines
candidates.privacy: material: runs on the host with access to messages
candidates.reason: Popularity is not evidence; host-level execution conflicts with the profile's security constraint and the owned stack already has scheduled agents.
candidates.reverify_trigger: security model hardened (default sandbox, permission model)

candidates.name: GitHub Copilot coding agent (Agent HQ)
candidates.job: assign GitHub issues to Copilot, Claude or Codex agents that open PRs
candidates.description: Agent HQ brings third-party agents into GitHub; Claude and Codex agents need Copilot Pro+ ($39/mo); billing moved to AI Credits on 2026-06-01.
candidates.evidence_notes: official announcement; pricing from secondary sources
candidates.reason: Would pay again for agents already owned directly (Claude Code, Codex).

candidates.name: Google Jules
candidates.job: asynchronous coding agent working on GitHub repos
candidates.description: Google's async coding agent; GA in 2026 with tiers tied to Google AI plans; a goal-driven V2 is reported.
candidates.evidence_notes: secondary sources only
candidates.reason: Duplicates owned background coding agents.

candidates.name: Claude Managed Agents
candidates.job: host your own persistent agent workers on Anthropic's runtime (or a self-hosted sandbox) without running servers
candidates.description: API service (public beta since 2026-04-08): token pricing plus $0.08 per active session-hour; self-hosted sandboxes in beta.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs; no independent reliability data
candidates.cost: API tokens + $0.08/active session-hour; Max/Team monthly API credits can offset
candidates.privacy: sessions run on Anthropic or your own sandbox
candidates.reason: The right substrate if a persistent worker or public tool gets built later; not a personal-use change now.
candidates.reverify_trigger: leaves beta

candidates.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
candidates.job: shrink shell command output (git, tests, builds, logs) before it enters the coding agent's context
candidates.description: Single Rust binary CLI proxy with a hook that rewrites agent Bash commands; supports Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and ~15 more agents.
candidates.evidence_notes: 60-90% is the project's own estimate (bytes/4); README admits bash output is one contributor to input tokens; only Bash calls are covered, not Read/Grep
candidates.cost: free (Apache-2.0 CLI; engine and proxy components BUSL-1.1)
candidates.permissions: hook rewrites every Bash command the agent runs; 'cargo install rtk' installs an unrelated crate
candidates.reason: Addresses tool-output cost, a larger share than output tokens; needs a with/without run on real sessions measuring task success and tokens.
candidates.reverify_trigger: independent benchmark or license change

candidates.name: Docling
candidates.job: convert PDF, Office, HTML, audio and image files into structured Markdown/JSON with tables and headings intact
candidates.description: Document conversion toolkit started at IBM Research; MIT; ships an MCP server.

sources.note: search-read; cites the OpenDataLoader 12-engine benchmark: Docling 0.882 overall

candidates.evidence_notes: independent 12-engine benchmark (via secondary write-up) ranks it top for structure fidelity
candidates.reason: Owned assistants read single PDFs fine; Docling is the gain for batch/structured conversion inside coding or research pipelines.

candidates.name: MarkItDown
candidates.job: fast file-to-Markdown text extraction
candidates.description: Microsoft's lightweight converter; much faster than Docling but drops structure.

sources.note: search-read; OpenDataLoader: 0.589 overall, 0.000 heading hierarchy, 0.273 table fidelity

candidates.evidence_notes: same independent benchmark; weak on headings and tables
candidates.reason: Docling covers the job with better structure; speed alone does not fit research/document work.

candidates.name: SkillsBench
candidates.capability: measuring whether an AI capability helps
candidates.job: measure whether a Skill actually raises task pass rates (no skill vs curated vs self-generated)
candidates.description: Peer-reviewed benchmark (NeurIPS 2026) of 84-87 tasks with deterministic verifiers; curated skills +16.2pp on average, self-generated skills about -1.3pp.
candidates.evidence_notes: peer-reviewed, deterministic verifiers, multiple models
candidates.reason: Gives a credible method (and evidence that focused, curated skills beat long docs) for every Skill candidate this scan marks benchmark-needed.

candidates.name: promptfoo
candidates.capability: measuring whether an AI capability helps
candidates.job: repeatable evals and red-team tests comparing prompts, models and agents on your own cases
candidates.description: MIT CLI/library for LLM evaluation; OpenAI announced its acquisition on 2026-03-09 and said it stays open source.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs and broad enterprise use; no independent comparison of eval harnesses found
candidates.privacy: local; calls the model APIs you configure
candidates.reason: Provider-neutral harness for the cross-model comparisons the evaluation job needs (Claude vs ChatGPT vs Codex outputs).
candidates.reverify_trigger: acquisition closes or license changes

candidates.name: Slidev
candidates.job: build technical slide decks as Markdown/Vue from a coding agent, with PDF/PPTX export
candidates.description: Open-source Markdown slide framework that ships official Skills for AI coding agents.
candidates.evidence_notes: official docs describe the agent workflow; practitioner reports only
candidates.reason: Alternative to native Claude Slides for code-heavy, version-controlled decks; compare both on one real deck.

candidates.name: OpenCode
candidates.job: open-source, provider-agnostic terminal coding agent
candidates.description: MIT coding agent (now under anomalyco/opencode); free, with optional paid model access tiers.
candidates.evidence_notes: secondary comparisons only
candidates.reason: Duplicates two owned coding agents; relevant only if open-weight models become a requirement.

candidates.name: Claude 5.5 model tiers (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku 5.5)
candidates.capability: model routing for cost and quality
candidates.job: route each task to the cheapest model that does it well (Haiku 5.5 for high-volume subagent work, Opus 5.5 for hard reasoning)
candidates.description: Opus 5.5 (2026-09-22; $4/$20 per M tokens; 1M context), Sonnet 5.5 (2026-09-28), Haiku 5.5 (2026-10-07, cheapest/fastest small model).
candidates.evidence_notes: official cards plus independent evaluations (Artificial Analysis, Vals); independent scores run below vendor scores
candidates.cost: included in Claude plans; API per-token
candidates.reason: Already owned; the opportunity is deliberate model routing to cut cost/limits. Measure quality on your own tasks before defaulting subagents to Haiku 5.5.
